statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 3 and far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z, leaving no Nasdaq-100 price path to score; the last observed path, Friday's record 31,017.53 intraday high fully retraced into a 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the 30,737.07-31,017.53 range with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31, is orderly two-way discovery rather than the extension pattern Tail measures. Stress is 72 in the high band because a record U.S. diesel squeeze, the G7's 100-million-barrel release, an officially unconfirmed fire at Aramco's Riyadh refinery, a verified tanker strike east of Oman and a 10-year that reversed higher to about 5.2939% on weak payrolls all remain unresolved with no venue able to price them. Confidence is 85 on independently re-verified session levels, H.15 yields, oil settlements, a now-verified tanker incident and a verified seven-day calendar, offset by the absence of any live price path.
recommendation: Tail remains in the low band for all 24 scored hours, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON and green throughout. Twenty-two of those hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt; the restart at 22:00Z on 4 October opens the twenty-third slot and the twenty-fourth slot is the first full hour of restored trading, which carries the window's highest Tail at 19. The Gulf cash session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z is the only live venue with direct exposure to the claimed Riyadh refinery strike; under the inherited delayed-evidence rule it can inform Stress and Confidence but cannot establish current Nasdaq-100 structure or the current action. A narrow danger window is published across the two reopening hours as a dated discontinuity checkpoint; it does not change the Tail-derived mapping. The next scheduled U.S. macro checkpoint is ISM Services at 14:00Z on 5 October, with FOMC minutes on 7 October.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 3 with no Nasdaq-100 price path to score, while a bounded Riyadh refinery fire, a verified Oman tanker strike and the G7's 100-million-barrel release keep Stress at 72 into the 22:00Z Sunday restart
body:
Friday 2 October remains the last traded session and its levels are independently re-verified for this publication. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range whose high is also the 52-week high. The detail that matters most for this framework is unchanged: the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced and the index finished in the lower quarter of its own daily range. That is orderly two-way price discovery, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39 and at the bottom of a 15.30-16.24 range, confirming volatility decay into the halt.

The session's driver was the September employment report, taken from the primary release: nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, the unemployment rate was 4.2%, and average hourly earnings edged up 0.1% to $37.81. Equities read that as cementing a Fed hold at the 28 October meeting, but the curve did not follow: the 10-year traded as low as 5.17% immediately after the data before reversing to about 5.2939%, roughly six basis points higher on the day, and the 2-year ended near 4.8414%. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%, so Friday's move extended an already elevated curve. A record equity close against rising long yields on weak labour data is a legitimate Stress and Confidence input; on this contract it is not a Tail input.

Two weekend threads that could not be verified at the previous publication are now resolved enough to score, and both resolve toward bounded rather than expanding risk. First, the Riyadh incident: a large plume of smoke and fire was reported near an Aramco facility south of the capital on Saturday, with the fire detected at roughly 05:00Z and firefighters on site, and the Houthi military spokesman claimed a ballistic-missile and drone strike in retaliation for Saudi air operations over Yemen that he put at 94 in 24 hours. Saudi authorities have still not confirmed an attack and Aramco has not commented on cause or damage. What is now clearer is scale: the Riyadh refinery is among the smallest in Saudi Arabia and serves domestic supply, and no disruption to refining throughput, production or exports has been confirmed. Second, the tanker report: a crude tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about four nautical miles east of Oman early Saturday, with all crew safe and no immediate environmental damage, and responsibility unattributed. Both are genuine escalation evidence and neither is a confirmed supply event.

The energy complex remains the dominant Stress driver and it is genuinely two-sided. The G7 and its partners agreed to a coordinated IEA release of 100 million barrels of oil and refined products over four months, frontloading a substantial diesel release inside the first 20 days, after the U.S. average diesel price reached record levels around $6.50 a gallon. Brent briefly fell below $100 on the announcement before settling Friday at $102.25, down 0.06%, while WTI settled at $91.11, down 1.90%. The IEA's director said prices had already fallen about $5 following the announcement, and cited expert views hold the effect will be short-lived against a persistent supply crunch. Pulling the other way, Saudi Arabia is reported to be preparing a broader offensive against Houthi forces, with options ranging from operations around Bab Al Mandab to multi-front action. Offsetting both, September LNG transits through the Strait of Hormuz reached their highest monthly level since the conflict began, at 19 cargoes including six from the UAE. The OPEC+ participating countries also meet online on 4 October to review November targets, widely expected to be left unchanged; because the exact hour is not reliably published it is carried as a driver checkpoint rather than a dated calendar event.

The window itself has advanced. The CME equity-index restart at 22:00Z on 4 October now opens the twenty-third scored hour, and the twenty-fourth slot is the first full hour of restored trading. Tail rises along the approach from 3 to 14 by 21:00Z, reaches 17 in the restart hour and 19 in the first full trading hour, remaining in the low band throughout because gap and thin-liquidity risk is a discontinuity rather than observed mean-reversion failure, and because no reopening level, gap direction or retracement behaviour has been observed. A gap alone would not raise Tail; a gap followed by shallow or failed retracements and repeated extension would be the first genuine Tail evidence of the week. The week ahead is moderate on U.S. macro: ISM Services on Monday, the trade balance, Williams and Bowman speeches and a 3-year auction on Tuesday, FOMC minutes and a 10-year auction on Wednesday, jobless claims and a 30-year auction on Thursday and preliminary Michigan sentiment on Friday, with the next rate decision not until 28 October. The shared Finviz context was again unusable for this run: it was collected on 29 September, roughly four days old against the 90-minute freshness bound, and is marked partial, so the assessment rests entirely on independent research and the evidence failed open as the contract requires.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments and no slot required an unavailable entry. The window opens at 00:00Z on 3 October with Tail 9 and Stress 68 under a normal mode and decays steadily as the halt takes hold: Tail falls from 9 to 3 by 12:00Z and stays at 3 for the remaining twelve hours. Stress troughs at 52 around 14:00Z and then climbs back to 71 by 23:00Z as the energy and Gulf escalation threads reopened and produced the claimed strike on a Riyadh refinery. Confidence held in a narrow 82 to 88 range throughout, consistent with verified session levels and no live price path. No historical opinion was revised.
outlookSummary: Twenty-two of the 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them. Tail is held at 3 through 09:00Z, then rises along the restart approach to 14 by 21:00Z, 17 in the 22:00Z restart slot and 19 in the first full hour of restored trading, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. Stress runs from 72 to a peak of 78 and stays in the high band before easing to 75 once a venue can price the weekend's news, because the G7 release, record diesel, a bounded Riyadh refinery fire, a verified Oman tanker strike and an elevated long end accumulate unresolved. Confidence eases from 85 to a low of 77 before the restart as Friday's levels age, lifting modestly during the Gulf cash session and recovering to 84 once live prices return. The dominant mode shifts to mixed four hours before the restart on two-sided catalysts rather than any observed directional bias. A narrow danger window marks the two reopening hours as a dated discontinuity checkpoint.
